summary: Fourteen days of high-quality CGM data show 86.0% time in range and an average glucose of 121.6 mg/dL, but 5.1% time below range and repeated values of 41–42 mg/dL make hypoglycemia the dominant concern. Afternoon rises are frequently followed by early-evening declines, while low exposure also recurs around midnight to 03:00 local time. The profile was declared applicable, but absent meal declarations and overlapping SMB, UAM, Dynamic ISF, corrections, temporary basal, targets, and IOB prevent attribution to one parameter. The safest synthesis is to keep all current profile and AAPS settings while reconstructing representative low and meal sequences before considering one isolated change.

analysis_steps.findings: CGM coverage supports time-of-day and safety-pattern analysis. The authoritative profile is complete and declared historically applicable. Meal, activity, rescue-carbohydrate, and full event-level insulin records are insufficient for isolating profile effects.
analysis_steps.evidence: There were 3,995 valid CGM readings, 98.7% coverage, an estimated five-minute cadence, no invalid or duplicate readings, ten gaps, and a largest gap of 65 minutes. The package contains all 17 profile items and all six AAPS decision groups.
analysis_steps.dependencies: Later conclusions depend on distinguishing observed telemetry from the empty user-declared meal strategy and from inferred meal effects.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Meal amounts and timing, prebolus and immediate-bolus declarations, e-carb declarations, activity, rescue carbohydrates, and complete insulin sequences around excursions are absent.

analysis_steps.findings: Recurrent hypoglycemia is the principal constraint. Hyperglycemia is concentrated in the afternoon, but reducing peaks without resolving subsequent insulin accumulation could worsen lows.
analysis_steps.evidence: Average glucose was 121.6 mg/dL, time in range 86.0%, time above range 8.9%, time below range 5.1%, and coefficient of variation 32.6%. Multiple readings reached 41–42 mg/dL. Local time below range was 18.5% at 01:00 and 15.3% at 19:00.
analysis_steps.dependencies: Every profile, automation, and meal-strategy decision depends on separating basal delivery from residual IOB, SMB/UAM, Dynamic ISF, corrections, activity, and temporary targets.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Fingerstick confirmation, symptoms, rescue treatment, activity, and complete preceding insulin delivery are unavailable.

analysis_steps.findings: Overnight and early-evening low exposure is real, but no basal or target segment is independently proven excessive. Afternoon highs do not establish insufficient basal because presumed meals and reactive automation remain plausible. The 18:00–19:00 basal increases and the 23:00 target reduction overlap low-risk periods but also overlap residual insulin from earlier highs.
analysis_steps.evidence: Local time below range was 10.1–18.5% from 23:00–03:00 and 15.3% at 19:00. Time above range peaked at 32.1% at 16:00. Basal changes to 0.5 U/h at 16:00, 0.6 U/h at 18:00, and 0.7 U/h at 19:00; the target changes from 100 to 90 mg/dL at 23:00.
analysis_steps.dependencies: Basal and target interpretation depends on full IOB and automation histories and on identifying fasting-like periods without meals, corrections, activity, or temporary targets.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No validated fasting-like test or complete operational target and IOB trace is supplied.

analysis_steps.findings: No CR segment can be assessed without meal-linked carbohydrate and bolus data. The static ISF cannot be isolated because Dynamic ISF materially changes effective sensitivity. The 10-hour DIA may preserve recognition of residual insulin, but overlapping delivery prevents validation of the action curve.
analysis_steps.evidence: There were zero carbohydrate entries. Profile CR ranges from 10.5 to 13.2 g/U. Profile ISF is 56 mg/dL/U, while sampled variable sensitivity ranged approximately from 27.8 to 124 mg/dL/U. Several correction windows showed large falls over two to six hours, but all were potentially confounded by additional insulin, food, or activity.
analysis_steps.dependencies: CR depends on meal execution data. ISF and DIA depend on Dynamic ISF, SMB/UAM, temporary basal, correction timing, and residual IOB.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Meal-linked dosing records and isolated correction or insulin-action observations are absent.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM are internally consistent and appear to respond reactively to unexplained rises with COB zero. This can permit post-rise hyperglycemia followed by cumulative insulin exposure. UAM is not duplicate COB counting. No single activation or delivery parameter is isolated sufficiently to support a change.
analysis_steps.evidence: SMB and UAM are enabled, SMB is always enabled, sampled loop records show COB zero, the SMB interval is configured at three minutes, and UAM permits 20 basal minutes versus 15 for standard SMB. Sampled IOB reached 4.73 U and 5.935 U during major highs.
analysis_steps.dependencies: Interpretation depends on meal timing, manual corrections, Dynamic ISF, high temporary basal, and the subsequent low sequences.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Complete SMB, temporary-basal, correction, IOB, and meal histories around each high-to-low event are absent.

analysis_steps.findings: Dynamic ISF materially strengthens effective correction sensitivity during some highs. The configured max basal and max IOB are permissive relative to the profile and observed use, but sampled operational limits were lower and neither configured maximum was shown to initiate the adverse sequences. Changing static ISF, Dynamic ISF, SMB limits, or safety ceilings together would prevent attribution.
analysis_steps.evidence: Dynamic sensitivity is enabled at 70%, while Autosens is disabled. Sampled variable sensitivity reached 37.9 mg/dL/U with 4.73 U IOB and 27.8 mg/dL/U with 5.935 U IOB. Configured limits are 12 U/h and 25 U, while sampled rates were limited near 4 U/h by other safety calculations.
analysis_steps.dependencies: Any sensitivity or limit review depends on reconstruction of insulin accumulation before lows and on separating food-driven rises from profile deficiencies.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: The package does not provide complete event-level sequences sufficient to identify which automation guardrail would have altered the adverse events.

analysis_steps.findings: The user-declared meal strategy is empty, while observed telemetry contains no carbohydrate entries or identifiable meal boluses. Presumed meal rises appear to be handled reactively through UAM, SMB, temporary basal, and corrections, but this remains an inference. No prebolus interval or immediate bolus percentage can be supported.
analysis_steps.evidence: The declared meal_strategies array is empty and strategy_stable_for_period is null. Treatment telemetry records zero carbohydrates and sampled loops show COB zero. Afternoon highs are followed by increased early-evening low exposure, and several correction windows show large delayed falls.
analysis_steps.dependencies: Assessment depends on CR, static and dynamic sensitivity, DIA, target, SMB/UAM, correction timing, and IOB.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Prebolus minutes, immediate bolus percentage, meal carbohydrate amount, meal timing, and identifiable meal insulin are absent.

analysis_steps.findings: Regular-carb versus e-carb handling cannot be evaluated. Prolonged glucose elevation cannot establish delayed absorption, and e-carbs cannot be inferred or treated as an extended pump bolus.
analysis_steps.evidence: There were zero carb entries, zero e-carb entries, no e-carb durations, and no carb timestamps. The configured minimum carb impact is 8 mg/dL per five minutes and maximum absorption time is seven hours, but entered-carbohydrate behavior was not observed.
analysis_steps.dependencies: Absorption assessment requires meal-linked carbohydrate declarations separated from corrections, SMB/UAM, temporary targets, IOB, and additional intake.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: E-carb amount, start offset, duration, meal composition, and meal-linked glucose responses are absent.

analysis_steps.findings: The leading explanation is reactive treatment of unexplained afternoon rises followed by cumulative insulin exposure, with evening basal and overnight targets remaining competing but unproven contributors. The evidence does not support a concrete profile or AAPS value change. The safe sequence is to keep settings, reconstruct severe-low sequences first, then review automation exposure, and only then evaluate a fully logged meal.
analysis_steps.evidence: High-quality CGM confirms recurring lows and afternoon high-to-low sequences, but the profile is complete, meal declarations are absent, and representative telemetry shows overlapping IOB, SMB/UAM, Dynamic ISF, temporary basal, corrections, and target changes.
analysis_steps.dependencies: A future parameter change should depend on repeated event-level evidence isolating one cause and should not coincide with changes to dependent settings.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: The most consequential missing observation is one complete six-hour sequence containing meal or fasting context, glucose, delivered insulin, IOB, SMB, temporary basal, corrections, activity, temporary target, and low treatment.

strengths: CGM data quality is high, with 98.7% coverage and no invalid or duplicate readings.
Overall time in range is 86.0%, and the coefficient of variation is below 36%.
The selected AAPS profile is complete and explicitly declared applicable to the analysis period.
The telemetry contains enough loop and treatment information to identify interactions among UAM, SMB, Dynamic ISF, temporary basal, and IOB, even though it cannot isolate one parameter.
issues: Time below range is 5.1%, with repeated glucose values of 41–42 mg/dL and concentrated low exposure around 19:00 and 23:00–03:00 local time.
Afternoon hyperglycemia is often followed by early-evening decline, suggesting possible cumulative insulin exposure rather than a simple isolated basal or CR defect.
Dynamic ISF sometimes produces substantially stronger effective sensitivity than the static 56 mg/dL/U ISF while SMB/UAM and temporary basal are also active.
The declared meal strategy is empty and telemetry records no carbohydrate or e-carb entries, preventing meal-linked assessment of CR, prebolus timing, immediate bolus percentage, or absorption.

recommendations.title: Primary: reconstruct severe-low insulin sequences before changing settings
recommendations.description: Keep the current profile and automation values while reviewing complete glucose, IOB, bolus, SMB, temporary-basal, target, activity, and low-treatment histories before the recurring 19:00 and overnight lows. This separates residual insulin from basal and target effects.

suggested_change.action: Keep all current values during verification
suggested_change.verification: Review at least two comparable low sequences with the preceding six hours of delivered insulin and context

recommendations.title: Evaluate cumulative automation only after event reconstruction
recommendations.description: If repeated low sequences show that SMB/UAM and Dynamic ISF accumulated insulin before basal suspension, review one automation component at a time. Do not simultaneously alter static ISF, Dynamic ISF, SMB limits, max IOB, or basal.

suggested_change.action: No automation value change supported yet
suggested_change.verification: Identify which delivery component contributed insulin before each repeated decline

recommendations.title: Log one complete representative meal before evaluating meal settings
recommendations.description: Record carbohydrate amount and time, insulin timing, immediate bolus percentage if used, any e-carb declaration, temporary target, corrections, SMB, IOB, and glucose through six hours. This is required before attributing afternoon rises to CR, prebolus timing, or absorption.

suggested_change.action: Do not introduce a new prebolus, immediate percentage, or e-carb value from this dataset
suggested_change.verification: Collect one complete meal-linked six-hour response

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep all current basal segments and the rest of the profile unchanged while retrospectively identifying at least two overnight or early-evening low sequences with six hours of complete IOB and delivered-insulin context.
profile_recommendation.rationale: Overnight and early-evening lows are reproducible, but basal, target, residual IOB, SMB/UAM, Dynamic ISF, corrections, activity, and low treatment are not separated. Afternoon highs also cannot justify stronger basal because they may represent presumed meals handled reactively.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Compare at least two low sequences after excluding or explicitly accounting for meals, corrections, activity, temporary targets, and substantial starting IOB.

parameter_decisions.rationale: Low exposure is elevated from midnight to 03:00, but residual evening IOB, the 90 mg/dL target, SMB/UAM, Dynamic ISF, and corrections remain unresolved. Keep pending repeated fasting-like or fully reconstructed overnight sequences.
Average glucose is broadly stable and aggregate low exposure falls after 04:00. One severe morning value does not isolate this segment because prior IOB and activity are unknown.
The 06:00–07:59 period has high aggregate time in range, but a 42 mg/dL minimum creates uncertainty. No fasting and IOB-controlled evidence supports a different value.
Morning rises overlap presumed meals, COB zero, UAM, Dynamic ISF, and the 08:00 target change. The data cannot separate insufficient basal from meal execution.

The highest aggregate glucose occurs near this segment, but subsequent evening lows and substantial automated IOB make an increase unsupported. Meal timing and reactive automation must be separated first.

This transition overlaps increasing low exposure, but insulin accumulated during preceding afternoon highs is an equally plausible cause. Complete pre-low delivery histories are required before changing basal.
Time below range is 15.3% at 19:00, but severe events follow periods of corrections, SMB/UAM, Dynamic ISF, and temporary basal. The segment cannot be isolated from residual IOB.
No meal-linked carbohydrate or bolus data exist for this segment. Overnight lows are not evidence of a CR defect without meal execution and IOB context.
Morning rises could involve meals, timing, target changes, or UAM, but zero carbohydrate entries prevent assessment of the ratio.
Morning and afternoon elevations are not linked to carbohydrate amounts, prebolus timing, or identifiable meal doses. CR cannot be separated from reactive automation.
This stronger ratio overlaps the afternoon high-to-evening-low sequence, but no associated meal bolus or carbohydrate amount is available. Both strengthening and weakening are unsupported.
Evening and overnight lows may reflect residual automated or correction insulin rather than meal dosing. Meal-linked evidence is absent.
Dynamic ISF changes effective sensitivity substantially, and correction windows contain overlapping insulin and possible food effects. The static ISF cannot be isolated.

Overnight low exposure makes this target relevant, but actual dosing also depends on residual IOB, temporary targets, SMB/UAM, Dynamic ISF, and basal. Operational target histories during lows are incomplete.
Daytime highs do not establish that this target is too high because meals and reactive automation are unresolved. Increasing dosing pressure could worsen later lows.
The change to 90 mg/dL overlaps elevated late-night low exposure, but preceding insulin and temporary-target context are not fully known. A value change requires repeated comparable sequences.

Observed glucose effects persist for several hours, but frequent overlapping insulin prevents measurement of an isolated action curve. DIA interacts with IOB recognition, SMB/UAM, and Dynamic ISF and should not change with those settings.

SMB/UAM respond to unexplained rises with COB zero and may contribute to cumulative IOB, but meals, corrections, Dynamic ISF, and temporary basal are not separated. Disabling both would be a dependent and unsupported change.

The switches are internally consistent and do not show duplicate COB dosing. Always-on SMB may increase exposure during unexplained rises, but event-level evidence does not isolate activation from SMB strength, UAM, Dynamic ISF, or corrections.

parameter_decisions.current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.rationale: The higher UAM allowance and three-minute opportunity interval may contribute to accumulation, but complete SMB histories are absent and temporary basal, corrections, and Dynamic ISF overlap. No supported replacement values can be derived.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS max basal and max IOB limits
parameter_decisions.rationale: These limits are permissive relative to profile basal and observed IOB, but sampled events were constrained by lower operational calculations and neither configured maximum was shown to trigger the adverse sequences. Changing both guardrails would not isolate the initiating mechanism.

Dynamic ISF materially strengthens sensitivity during some highs and is a plausible contributor to IOB accumulation, while Autosens is correctly represented as disabled. Static ISF, SMB/UAM, temporary basal, and corrections remain dependent confounders, so no isolated new value is supported.
No regular-carb or e-carb entries exercised the entered-carbohydrate model during the period. Prolonged glucose changes cannot be attributed to absorption without meal-linked evidence.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Keep prebolus minutes and immediate bolus percentage unspecified, keep current SMB/UAM settings unchanged, and do not introduce an e-carb amount or duration from this dataset. First document one representative meal with its carbohydrate entry, insulin timing, immediate percentage if used, any e-carb amount, offset and duration, and the complete six-hour automation and IOB response.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: The declared meal strategy is empty and observed telemetry contains no carbohydrate entries, while UAM appears to respond reactively with COB zero. Afternoon highs followed by evening lows could reflect delayed meal handling and cumulative insulin, but CR, ISF, DIA, target, SMB/UAM, corrections, and temporary basal cannot be separated.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Capture one meal with carbohydrate amount and timestamp, prebolus interval, immediate bolus percentage, any e-carb declaration, temporary target, corrections, SMB, temporary basal, IOB, and glucose through six hours.

exceptions.pattern: Afternoon high followed by early-evening decline
exceptions.suggestion: Do not make the late-afternoon prebolus, immediate percentage, CR, SMB/UAM, or e-carb strategy more aggressive until the complete six-hour insulin sequence is reviewed.
exceptions.rationale: This recurring period combines the highest time above range with later severe-low risk and overlaps the 16:00 CR, Dynamic ISF, UAM, corrections, and basal transitions.

exceptions.pattern: Morning rise without the same concentrated immediate low pattern
exceptions.suggestion: Evaluate a separately logged morning meal rather than applying conclusions from the afternoon sequence.
exceptions.rationale: The 08:00 target, 10:00 basal transition, presumed meal timing, and reactive UAM create a different set of dependencies.

implementation_steps: Keep the current profile and AAPS values unchanged during the initial review.

Reconstruct at least two severe or recurring low sequences using the preceding six hours of glucose, delivered insulin, IOB, SMB, temporary basal, correction, target, activity, and low-treatment information.
Determine whether the repeated lows begin with substantial residual IOB, occur during fasting-like conditions, or follow a specific automation component.
If one cause is reproduced, review only that single profile or automation parameter while holding dependent settings constant.
After the low pattern is understood, collect one fully logged representative meal and review its six-hour response before considering CR, prebolus, immediate bolus percentage, or e-carbs.
Independently verify any future proposed change, make only one change at a time, and monitor glucose closely.
education: High time in range can coexist with excessive hypoglycemia; recurrent values near 41–42 mg/dL take priority over reducing moderate post-meal peaks.
A low after a high does not by itself identify excessive basal. Insulin delivered earlier by SMB, UAM, temporary basal, Dynamic ISF, or corrections can continue acting after basal is suspended.
Dynamic ISF can make effective sensitivity substantially stronger than the static profile ISF, so static ISF cannot be interpreted alone.
UAM responds to unexplained glucose rises when COB is zero; it is not automatic duplicate counting of entered carbohydrates.
E-carbs describe carbohydrate absorption for the algorithm and are not equivalent to an extended pump bolus.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only and does not provide medical advice.
The user must independently verify every proposed change, make changes one at a time, and monitor glucose closely.
Repeated glucose values of 41–42 mg/dL warrant prompt review with the diabetes care team and confirmation according to the user's established safety plan.
No AAPS or profile setting should be changed automatically from this analysis.
